summary: Round 2 re-review of fd63dfb3. All three findings from round 1 are closed and I found no regressions. CR-R1-01 (critical, blocking) is closed: runner.py:20 imports `cache, condition_cache, counters, evidence` again, so the post-loop `final_cache = cache(...)` call at runner.py:202 resolves. The new test_port.unresolved_globals check walks the LOAD_GLOBAL instructions in runner.execute and every nested code object, which covers the nested functions and generator expressions. It compares those names against module globals and builtins. The positive test asserts nothing is left unresolved. The negative control deletes `cache` and confirms the check reports it, so the check would have caught the original regression. I also checked by hand every global name in execute: each is imported or a builtin, and the names imported inside execute (MPI, cp, np, defaults, kvikio, EventManager, accounting, etc.) are locals or closure variables, not globals. CR-R1-02 (low) is closed: validate_cache_gate now requires the verify scan to complete at least 0.1s (CACHE_VERIFY_PAUSE) minus 1us after the evict scan. It also requires a retry's evict scan to complete at least 1s (CACHE_RETRY_PAUSE) minus 1us after the previous verify scan. The audit deadline is now strict (<180), the same as runtime. The runtime ordering always meets these limits, because each recorded completion time includes the pause plus the scan time. These checks are lower bounds on completion-time spacing and do not prove how long the sleeps actually took. New corruption tests cover the verify gap, the retry gap and the exact-180 deadline, and the existing 3-attempt positive audit still passes. CR-R1-03 (low) is closed: comparison.build takes the attempt count and conditioning_seconds from each re-audited, hash-checked report. summarize checks those values against the policy limits and emits 35 ordered cache_conditioning records. The processing statistics do not change, and the interpretation text says conditioning is excluded from processing. This verdict rests on coordinator-supplied host evidence: 164 passed and 64 subtests passed at this exact HEAD, with source hashes matching. Neither GPU, Lustre nor scheduler execution has been qualified, and it is still unknown whether three attempts will clear the job61391587 residency failure.

It subtracts function.__globals__ and builtins. The positive test asserts the result is empty, and the negative control monkeypatch.delitem(runner.__dict__, 'cache') asserts that 'cache' is detected. Against the c2667aa import line, the positive test would fail.

Coordinator evidence for this exact HEAD fd63dfb3: 164 passed and 64 subtests passed, task status clean, and the runner.py, storage.py, comparison.py, test_port.py, test_storage.py and test_comparison.py hashes are listed as matching. I treat this as supplied evidence and did not run anything.
limitations: I had no shell, so I ran no tests, imports, disassembly or hash checks. All execution results come from the coordinator's evidence.

The bytecode global check covers only runner.execute and its nested code. Other bundled entry points (campaign.py, prepare.py, clean_exec.py, comparison.build) are not covered. Their names were checked only by reading, and only for comparison.py, which looks correct. It also cannot catch locals used before assignment or attribute errors, which are rank-branch dependent in runner.execute. I read those paths by hand and found nothing wrong.
The spacing audit checks completion-time differences, which include scan time. These are necessary lower bounds and do not independently prove the actual sleep durations.

No GPU, Lustre or Slurm run of the new conditioning path has happened, and the job61391587 residency failure has not been diagnosed. Host tests do not show that Lustre eviction will succeed in three attempts.

I did not re-read in full the parts of plan.py, campaign.py, run.sbatch, prepare.py, clean_exec.py, test_boundaries.py, AUTHORIZATION.md or the job61391587 result artifacts that are unchanged since round 1. Round 1's conclusions about them are carried forward.
